quizzes.title: CETA Scope and Entry into Force: Context
quizzes.passage: The India-UK agreement was pursued in a changing trade environment. After Brexit, the UK lost its access to the EU market and began seeking new trade partnerships for growth and global market access. India's growing economy positions it as a key trade partner for the UK after Brexit. Many Western nations have also moved to diversify their trade away from China, citing supply chain and geopolitical concerns. Under this approach, India is treated as a China-plus-one alternative, and a free trade agreement is central to the diversification strategy. India is also seeking to diversify its trade partners and reduce its dependence on China. Its bilateral free trade agreements, including the one with the UK, are presented as a way to safeguard its interests. Global uncertainty adds to the case. US tariffs and geopolitical tensions are pushing nations towards stable and predictable trade relations. The agreement is described as offering a stable trade framework that ensures economic predictability and long-term growth amid that uncertainty. The agreement itself is described as a next-generation free trade agreement. It goes beyond conventional tariff reduction, and the booklet presents it as a framework for wider economic partnership. Its coverage is wide, and it is presented as a step in India's broader trade realignment.

questions.q: How did India safeguard its generic pharmaceutical sector in the FTA with the UK?
options: By imposing higher import duties on branded medicines
By excluding Data Exclusivity provisions from the FTA
By mandating technology transfer from UK pharma companies
By restricting UK pharma companies from patenting in India
questions.explanation: The booklet says India excluded Data Exclusivity from the FTA to safeguard its generic pharma sector.

questions.q: What does the quota-based approach to imported passenger vehicles achieve?
options: It completely removes all tariffs on imported passenger vehicles
It bans imports of passenger vehicles for five years
It allows unrestricted import of electric vehicles only
It protects domestic industry while allowing phased market access
questions.explanation: The booklet says the tariff rate quota approach protects domestic industry while allowing phased market access.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Most of India's tariff lines are expected to become tariff-free within 10 years under the FTA.
Reason (R): 85% of tariff lines become tariff-free in 10 years.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The 85% figure for tariff-free lines within 10 years is the stated basis for the claim that most lines become tariff-free.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Imported passenger vehicles   ->   A. Concession through tariff rate quotas
II. Auto import tariff   ->   B. Cut to 10% under the quota system
III. Whisky and gin   ->   C. Cut from 150% to 75% initially
IV. Visas for Indian professionals   ->   D. 100 additional annual visas
questions.explanation: Each item matches its own concession: vehicles to tariff rate quotas, auto tariff to 10%, whisky and gin to 75% initially, and visas to 100 per year.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the India-UK CETA:
I. It covers digital trade and investment.
II. It is limited to tariff reduction on goods.
III. It covers labour, environment and SMEs.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists digital trade, investment, labour, environment and SMEs as covered, while the CETA goes beyond tariff reduction, so statement II is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the India-UK CETA:
I. It covers government procurement.
II. It covers regulatory cooperation.
III. It excludes investment.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Government procurement and regulatory cooperation are covered, but investment is also covered, so only statements I and II are correct.

questions.q: Beyond conventional tariff reduction, the CETA addresses which of the following?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the CETA goes beyond conventional tariff reduction by addressing market access, regulatory transparency and economic partnership.

questions.q: On which date did the India-UK CETA come into force? (give day, month and year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the CETA came into force on 15 July 2026.

questions.q: Under the quota system, India's auto import tariff falls to what percentage from over 100%? (number only, in %)
questions.explanation: The booklet says India cuts auto import tariffs to 10% under the quota system, down from over 100%.

questions.q: Whisky and gin tariffs are initially cut from 150% to what percentage? (number only, in %)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the whisky and gin tariff is cut from 150% to 75% initially.

questions.q: By the 10th year, the tariff on whisky and gin is reduced to what percentage? (number only, in %)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the whisky and gin tariff reduces to 40% by the 10th year.

questions.q: What percentage of India's tariff lines become tariff-free within 10 years? (number only, in %)
questions.explanation: The booklet says 85% of tariff lines become tariff-free in 10 years.

questions.q: How many additional annual visas does the FTA provide for Indian professionals? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists 100 additional annual visas for Indian professionals under the FTA.

questions.q: Which provision did India exclude from the FTA with the UK to safeguard its generic pharma sector? (name it in two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says India excluded Data Exclusivity from the FTA with the UK to protect its generic pharma sector.

quizzes.title: Double Contribution Convention: Context
quizzes.passage: A trade pact between two countries has been described as a next-generation free trade agreement. It goes beyond conventional tariff reduction and deals with market access, regulatory transparency and economic partnership. Its scope covers trade in goods and services, digital trade, investment, government procurement, labour, environment, innovation, SMEs and regulatory cooperation. Alongside the trade pact, the two countries signed a Double Contribution Convention Agreement. The Convention sits alongside the pact as a separate instrument. The booklet discusses it in a separate box alongside the trade pact. Wider context in the booklet relates to these trade arrangements. After leaving the EU, the UK lost its access to the EU market and sought new trade partnerships for growth and global market access. Western nations have also moved to diversify trade away from China because of supply chain and geopolitical concerns. US tariffs and geopolitical tensions have pushed nations towards stable and predictable trade relations. The booklet presents such pacts as offering economic predictability and long-term growth amid global uncertainty, and it describes the wider Brexit background as the UK leaving the European Union, an economic and political union of 28 European countries. It allows free trade among member countries without any checks or extra charges. Britain has faced many more challenges while sacrificing the smooth and frictionless flow of goods across its borders.

questions.q: On which date did the Double Contribution Convention Agreement come into force?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Convention came into force on 15 July 2026, along with CETA.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the Double Contribution Convention?
options: To ensure professionals avoid paying social security contributions in both India and the UK
To give Indian employers duty-free access to UK markets
To grant 100 additional visas to Indian professionals
To set up a common currency between India and the UK
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Convention ensures professionals avoid paying social security contributions in both India and the UK.

questions.q: For up to how many years does the exemption from UK National Insurance contributions apply?
questions.explanation: The booklet says eligible persons are exempt from UK National Insurance contributions for up to 5 years.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Eligible Indian employers can be exempted from UK National Insurance contributions.
Reason (R): The Convention's exemption covers eligible Indian professionals and employers.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The reason states that the exemption covers eligible employers, which is the basis of the assertion.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Eligible beneficiaries   ->   A. Professionals and employers
II. Contributions exempted   ->   B. UK National Insurance
III. Maximum exemption period   ->   C. Up to 5 years
IV. Condition for exemption   ->   D. Contributions continue in India
questions.explanation: The booklet links professionals and employers to the exemption, UK National Insurance to the contributions, up to 5 years to the period, and continuation in India to the condition.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Double Contribution Convention:
I. The exemption from UK National Insurance contributions can last up to 5 years.
II. The exemption continues even if contributions stop being paid in India.
III. The exemption is available only to professionals, not employers.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since the exemption requires contributions to continue in India and covers employers as well as professionals.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Double Contribution Convention:
I. Eligible Indian professionals are exempted from UK National Insurance contributions.
II. The exemption can run for 10 years.
III. Social security contributions must continue in India for the exemption.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II is wrong because the exemption runs for up to 5 years.

questions.q: On which date did the Double Contribution Convention Agreement come into force? (give day, month and year)

questions.q: Eligible professionals and employers are exempted from which UK contributions? (name the scheme)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the exemption covers UK National Insurance contributions.

questions.q: For up to how many years does the exemption apply? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the exemption applies for up to 5 years.

questions.q: Apart from professionals, which other eligible group is exempted? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says eligible Indian professionals and employers are both exempted.

questions.q: What kind of contributions do professionals avoid paying in both countries? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Convention ensures professionals avoid paying social security contributions in both India and the UK.

questions.q: Under the exemption, contributions must continue in which country? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the exemption applies provided social security contributions continue in India.

questions.q: Along with which agreement did the Double Contribution Convention come into force? (abbreviation)
